bull.b: Early human data support continued development of a brain-penetrant, wholly owned NLRP3 inhibitor. Demonstrated target exposure and tolerability may broaden AC Immune’s pipeline beyond established protein targets and improve future partnering potential.

Fast Track and IND clearance enable broader U.S. Phase 2 development of a proprietary Parkinson’s program. Sustained clinical advancement could strengthen AC Immune’s disease-modifying franchise and create additional strategic value.

The Takeda agreement provides non-product funding and preserves substantial milestone and royalty potential. This partnership model can finance development while giving AC Immune commercial leverage through an established pharmaceutical partner.

bear.b: AC Immune has not yet demonstrated operating leverage: revenue remains volatile and small relative to expenses while losses persist. Continued dependence on collaborations and external capital increases execution risk as programs advance.

The return to substantial cash consumption indicates that current operations do not self-fund research and development. Unless collaboration receipts or financing offset the burn, future clinical progress may require additional capital.

Low debt limits immediate leverage risk, but the sharply reduced equity base reflects accumulated losses and weakens financial resilience. A smaller cushion leaves less room to absorb trial setbacks or prolonged development spending.
